method: Read each cited source line with surrounding subsection context, not as an isolated candidate.
Distinguish obligations on file producers from requirements on VCF-compliant readers.
Split independently testable constraints into separate atomic requirements.
Treat declarative format properties and negative formulations such as 'not allowed' as discovery targets even when no modal token is present.
Do not infer applicability to VCFv4.0–4.2 from VCFv4.3–4.5; unresolved versions remain unresolved until their own authoritative source is checked.

findings: The sentence stating that a single fileformat field/line is always required and must be first contains at least two independently testable obligations: presence/uniqueness and first-line position.
The following example fixes the version-specific literal declaration value; the example is evidence for version identity, not an additional independent requirement.

The preceding meta-information paragraph states that other meta-information lines may appear in any order except fileformat, supporting the first-line rule and distinguishing it from general metadata ordering.
The UTF-8 statement is a declarative format constraint and is not found by the existing modal-word matcher.
The byte-order-mark prohibition is independently testable.
The disallowed control-character ranges are a distinct prohibition and must not be conflated with the BOM rule.
The line-separator sentence defines both the allowed newline encodings and their placement. It is decomposed into allowed LF/CRLF support and prohibition of separator characters inside line content.
The opening-section zero-length-field prohibition is another non-modal-language discovery case.
Header and data field tab-delimitation are declarative serialization constraints across the reviewed VCFv4.1–4.5 passages; they are not discovered by a modal-word-only matcher.
Duplicate sample identifiers are prohibited in the reviewed VCFv4.1–4.5 passages using 'not allowed' wording, which the existing modal matcher does not recognize.
The header and data-line trailing-tab prohibitions are separately observable and separately testable.
The requirement for the last data line to end with a line separator is a producer/file conformance constraint distinct from the reader's LF/CRLF support requirement.
These constraints occur in prose without being represented by the candidate intake as separate atomic records; discovery must inspect source structure and context, not only candidate counts.

decomposition_decisions.candidate: VCFv4.1:L0059 and equivalent fileformat lines in 4.2-4.5
decomposition_decisions.result: Retain separate atomic obligations for declaration presence/uniqueness and first-line position; do not treat example text as another requirement.
Keep newline repertoire/support separate from separator-placement prohibition.
Create a non-modal candidate for zero-length-field prohibition.
Create a non-modal declarative encoding constraint.
Create separate BOM and control-character prohibitions.
Create separate trailing-tab constraints for header and data lines and a final-data-line terminator constraint.

decomposition_decisions.candidate: VCFv4.1:L0155/L0159 and corresponding header/data passages in 4.2–4.5
decomposition_decisions.result: Create separate requirements for tab-delimited header fields, tab-delimited data fields, and unique sample identifiers; they are independently testable.
